paper_identity: PDF is Wen B, Zhang N, Jin S-R, Chen Z-Z, Gao J-Z, Liu Y, Liu H-P, Xu Z (2018) "Microplastics have a more profound impact than elevated temperatures on the predatory performance, digestion and energy metabolism of an Amazonian cichlid", Aquatic Toxicology 195: 67-76 (doi 10.1016/j.aquatox.2017.12.010). This matches the sheet metadata exactly: author Wen, year 2018, Actinopterygii, Symphysodon aequifasciatus, discus fish. Note the same lab's companion paper Wen et al. 2017 is a separate study in the same sheet (s23, 20/24 vs 28 degC), and the two must not be conflated - s99 is the 28 vs 31 degC x microplastic paper.
error_statistic_reported: The paper NEVER states what the error bars are. I grepped the full text: there is no "mean +/- SD", no "SEM", no "standard deviation/error" statement anywhere; Methods 2.9 (p.4) describes only Kolmogorov-Smirnov, Levene, two-way ANOVA and Bonferroni; the legends of Figs 1-6 explain only the letter codes. The only "+/-" in the paper is the husbandry water temperature (28.0 +/- 1.0 degC, p.3). The extractor's note says the authors confirmed by email that the bars are SD, and I can corroborate that independently: reconstructing the 2x2 ANOVA from the digitised cell means with the plotted bars treated as SDs and n = 3 reproduces Table 1 almost exactly for ALP (predicted F_T 979 / F_MP 96.9 / F_int 3.51 vs reported 924.654 / 91.655 / 3.248), ETS (0.162 / 1.42 / 2.95 vs 0.151 / 1.451 / 2.893) and CS (17.3 / 9.6 / 3.6 vs 13.937 / 7.448 / 2.911). If the bars were SEM the implied MSE would be 3x too large and these F values would be ~3x too small. So sd_* is correctly holding an SD (sd = se*sqrt(n) convention is internally consistent in the sheet, se_* = sd_*/sqrt(60)) - EXCEPT that the sqrt(n) used was 60 (finding 1), and except for LDH, where the plotted bars cannot be SDs, SEMs or CIs consistent with Table 1 (finding 3).
stated_sample_sizes: The paper never prints an "n =" for the enzyme assays. Methods 2.3 (p.3) states: "a total of 240 full-sibling juvenile S. aequifasciatus individuals were randomly distributed among 50-L tanks (20 fish per tank, three tanks per treatment)". The extractor read 20 x 3 = 60 fish per treatment and entered n_t1 = n_t2 = 60. The unit of replication in the analysis is the tank/sample, n = 3 per treatment cell, not 60: every p value in Table 1 (p.4) is exactly the F(1,8) tail probability (SR F=0.036 p=0.855 -> 0.8542; PEPP F=9.389 p=0.015 -> 0.0155; trypsin int F=2.846 p=0.130 -> 0.1301; amylase T F=24.180 p=0.001 -> 0.0012; ALP int F=3.248 p=0.109 -> 0.1092; ETS T F=0.151 p=0.708 -> 0.7077; ETS MP F=1.451 p=0.263 -> 0.2628; LDH T F=1.883 p=0.207 -> 0.2072; LDH int F=8.612 p=0.019 -> 0.0189; CS T F=13.937 p=0.006 -> 0.0058; CS MP F=7.448 p=0.026 -> 0.0259; COX MP F=7.688 p=0.024 -> 0.0242; COX int F=0.755 p=0.410 -> 0.4102). Fitting error df across 14 of these p values, df2 = 8 is a near-exact fit (summed absolute p error 0.004) and every other df is much worse (df2 = 9 -> 0.037, df2 = 236 -> 0.303). Error df = 8 in a 2x2 design means 3 replicates per cell. Independent confirmation: with n = 3 the ALP temperature F reconstructs as 979 (reported 925); with n = 60 it would be ~19,600. The same lab's companion study in this same sheet (s23, Wen et al. 2017) was coded n = 3. So n_t1 and n_t2 do NOT match the paper.
temperature_treatments: Two temperatures: ambient/control 28 degC and elevated 31 degC (+3 degC, the IPCC near-future projection; Methods 2.3, p.3). 28 degC is unambiguously the correct reference: broodstock and larvae were held at 28.0 +/- 1.0 degC (Methods 2.2) and the paper cites Pirhonen et al. (2014) that juvenile S. aequifasciatus grow optimally at 28-29 degC. The sheet assigns t1 = 31 (treatment) and t2 = 28 (control) with dose = 3 degC, which is correct for all 5 rows.
multiple_stressors: Yes - a full 2 x 2 crossing of temperature (28 vs 31 degC) with microplastics (0 vs 200 ug/L polyethylene microspheres, 70-88 um; Methods 2.1, 2.3). All 5 sheet rows were taken from the dark bars, i.e. the 0 ug/L (microplastic-free) baseline level of the second factor, in both the 28 and 31 degC groups. I verified this bar-by-bar against Figs 5D and 6A-D: the light (200 ug/L) bars are 453/202 for ALP, 6.29/5.03 for ETS, ~135.5/~124.5 for LDH, 5.95/5.18 for CS and ~39/~30 for COX, none of which appear in the sheet. So criterion 4 is satisfied and no row comes from a non-baseline level. There is no drug/supplement co-treatment, and microplastic-free animals exist, so criterion 3 is not triggered.
developmental_timing: Correct. Fish were full-sibling juveniles (0+ group) moved to experimental tanks at one week post-hatch and the exposure began one week later, i.e. at 14 days post-hatch, and ran 30 days to day 44 (Methods 2.3: "At one week post-hatch, which was one week before the beginning of the experiment..."; "After 30 days of experimental exposure, fish survival and individual body lengths were determined, after which fish were sacrificed"). The sheet's post_natal_trt_start = 14, postnatal_trt_end = 44, dur_trt_postnatal = 30 days and total_trt_duration = 30 days are therefore right, as is postnatal_measure_delay = 0 (tissues were taken immediately at the end of exposure). Symphysodon aequifasciatus reaches sexual maturity at roughly 12-18 months (the sheet's own note for the companion study s23), so 14-44 days post-hatch is entirely pre-sexual-maturity and the treatment does not span into maturity. sex = "both" is a reasonable default since the paper does not sex the juveniles.
